newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says economy continuing gradual recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says economy continuing gradual recovery.

text.p: The Japanese economy is continuing its gradual recovery, with private demand becoming increasingly firm, the Bank of Japan said in its monthly economic review on Friday.

The BOJ has not changed its view that the economy is continuing to grow gradually, but is generally more optimistic following the recent release of economic indicators, said Takayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department.
The report said the pace of the rise in industrial output is increasing and that private consumption is continuing its moderate increase.
The report also said the decline in Japan's net exports has bottomed out, which Matsushima described as the impact of the weakening yen.

He declined to comment directly on the recent fall in the Tokyo stock market, but added "we (the department) are closely following the moves of the financial markets, but there were times in the past when there was a discrepancy between the real economy and the financial markets' views of the economy."
Matsushima also said he does not have a clear outlook yet for Japan's future economy.
"The number of bright indicators are increasing but there are still some which are weak," he said.
